parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both services deal with fleet upkeep, so the module's concern hangs together well enough. The two files do not reach persistence the same way, though. MaintenanceService goes only through the table/repository abstractions VehicleTable and WorkOrderTable. It gets rows from row(), turns them into domain objects (Vehicle, WorkOrder) and saves through write() and insert(). MileageService skips that pattern. It injects PrismaService and calls the ORM delegates prisma.mileage.create and prisma.mileage.findMany itself, inside the business layer, with no mileage table or repository in between. I confirmed both candidate flags (lines 8 and 13) in the source. They show the ORM client being used directly, around the persistence abstraction the module uses elsewhere. MileageService also skips the Vehicle domain object. It takes a raw lastServiceKm and writes the service-due check out by hand as km - lastServiceKm >= SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM, using the constant imported from Vehicle, instead of asking a Vehicle. The source for Vehicle is not shown, so I can't confirm a copied rule. But the check is written in full here instead of being a call to one shared definition. The rubric fails a unit that does not use its abstractions consistently and that reaches the ORM directly, so the unit fails.

violations.message: MileageService skips the module's table/repository abstraction that MaintenanceService uses (VehicleTable, WorkOrderTable). It injects PrismaService and calls prisma.mileage.create and prisma.mileage.findMany directly, so a business service reaches the ORM itself.

record() writes out the service-due check by hand (km - lastServiceKm >= SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM) on a raw lastServiceKm parameter. It does not go through the Vehicle domain object, which skips the module's domain abstraction for that rule.
